articles.title: Uber’s Legal AI Agent Cuts Contract Review Time by 20% with Rules and RAG
articles.summary: Uber’s Legal Redlining Agent reviews contract changes in Microsoft Word using RAG, historical lawyer feedback, and deterministic policy rules. Built with LangGraph, OpenSearch, and Redis, the system r...
articles.description: Uber’s Legal Redlining Agent reviews contract changes in Microsoft Word using RAG, historical lawyer feedback, and deterministic policy rules. Built with LangGraph, OpenSearch, and Redis, the system reports more than 20% lower average contract review time and 91% accuracy in AI-generated decisions. Uber is exploring agentic harnesses, skills, legal ontologies, and knowledge graphs. By Leela Kumili

articles.title: Learning with the system: breaking down the silos in how we learn and grow
Airbnb Introduces CASTLE for Training Natural Language Search Models with Synthetic Data
articles.summary: Airbnb researchers have introduced CASTLE, a framework designed to address the cold-start problem in natural language search. The approach uses de-identified booking sessions and large language models...
articles.description: Airbnb researchers have introduced CASTLE, a framework designed to address the cold-start problem in natural language search. The approach uses de-identified booking sessions and large language models (LLMs) to jointly generate synthetic search queries and relevance labels, enabling model training before sufficient real search traffic is available. By Robert Krzaczyński

articles.title: Article: Governed Autonomous Intelligence for Mission-Critical Utility
articles.summary: The article describes an architecture for agentic AI in regulated utility operations. Agents reason and propose actions, but a deterministic policy gate and a governed tool gateway control execution, ...
articles.description: The article describes an architecture for agentic AI in regulated utility operations. Agents reason and propose actions, but a deterministic policy gate and a governed tool gateway control execution, with human approval where required. It covers an AWS reference implementation, grounding in runbooks, governed prediction, outcome validation, audit evidence, and phased autonomy. By Purnang Borah
